title: The Lunceford style and teaching six-part harmony
summary: Lunceford was a novelty band with dancers, glee club and trio; Durham voiced six-part harmony for a five-horn section and left because pay stopped at $60-65.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Now, how did that sort of Lunceford style -- I mean, the style of the thing, how did that hit you? Did you like it?
Well, the music wasn't all that great, but they just had a variety of novelty.
Dancing, they had a dancing chorus. Six of the guys come out and do the dance.
(Unintelligible) they'd come out and do a whole routine with the chorus boys. By the time they'd get back, there's the glee club and they had a trio.

So then, I was the guy that could really voice that harmony for myself, because they didn't have but five horns and they weren't writing for six horns. So that's why the repertoire was short on my part, when the trombone went in my place.

Lunceford told me we have to teach him. Three weeks and you can lead the band, I didn't know you could lead anyway. Because there wasn't that much music. So they just started -- let him do a lot of solo work and then we don't have to worry too much, because you see, the guys wasn't writing good harmony in those days, not six-part. So I had to kind of get
in there and work Wilcox and Sy and all of them with that six-part harmony.
So that's how I got in Lunceford's band. And the reason I left Lunceford, because he never did get me no further than $60, $65 a week. And I joined Basie for $150.
